test.name: A bounded interpretive ask hands off to historical-context, not the records job
test.description: Issue #4381, lead ruling 2026-11-09: why a move or event in the family happened, what could explain a pattern in it, or historical background for either, is a bounded deliverable owned by @plugin:historical-context. Feedback #4300 asked 'For the children of PID L6KS-9PW, Daniel Cook, can you explain what could be behind the migration patterns?'; question-selection turned it into a records question, and the run made 11 locality surveys and 2 plans and never answered it. The same tester's #3244 and #3930 asks went the same way. The scenario has no questions, so the job path's first hand-off is question-selection. Its tree holds Patrick Flynn with no facts and no children, so the delegation should say the tree holds none. It may add the objective's 1845 and 1908 named as the objective's (Ikennaya, 2026-11-17, after 3 of 3 scratch runs passed them that way); delegates-tree-facts fails any other year.

judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST ROUTING test. The message asks for ONE deliverable on the skill's bounded list, and its owner is historical-context. A deterministic validator (test_routes_to_expected_skill) asserts the first hand-off is historical-context. Do not grade the routing decision yourself.

The deliverable is a historical explanation of what could be behind the Flynn children's migration. The owner is historical-context. Answering it in the reply, or from the project objective, is wrong.

DO NOT REQUIRE ANY OTHER STEP FIRST. Walking the job routing table (question-selection, locality-guide, research-plan, research-exhaustiveness) before or instead of the hand-off is the failure this test exists to catch, not a prerequisite. Doing the deliverable's work inline is also a failure. A tree_query call before the hand-off is not inline work: the router reads the places and years it hands over.

THE TREE HOLDS NO FACTS for Patrick Flynn and no children, so a delegation saying the tree holds none is correct, and so is passing the project objective's places and years named as the objective's. Deterministic validators check that the spawn carries the user's message verbatim and no year beyond the tree, the message and the objective.

EVERY CALLEE IS STUBBED, so nothing is written to the project. '(no research.json or tree.gedcomx.json changes)' is the EXPECTED state and is NOT a fabricated claim. The run ends at the first stubbed hand-off by design (execution.stop_at_stub), with no closing summary: do not mark a summary as missing.

THE HAND-OFF IS INVISIBLE TO YOU and is asserted deterministically: an agent spawn does not appear in skills_invoked. Do not conclude from its absence that the router did its own work. Grade only the router's own narration up to the hand-off: honest, and free of internal ids shown to the user.

PROJECT_LIST FIRST IS REQUIRED. When no projectPath is named, the router's first call is project_list with no arguments, to find the project. It is not a step before the hand-off, not inline work and not a call missing an argument; its folder answer is the live tool's real answer, not an error.
